questions.prompt_text: Read the extract and complete the activities given below: At length Soapy reached one of the avenues to the east where the glitter and turmoil was but faint. He dragged himself toward Madison Square, for the homing instinct survives even when the home is a park bench. But, on an unusually quiet corner, Soapy came to a standstill. Here was an old church, quaint and rambling and gabled. Through one violet-stained window a soft light glowed, where, no doubt, the organist loitered over the keys, making sure of his mastery of the coming Sabbath Anthem. For there drifted out to Soapy’s ears sweet music that caught and held him transfixed against the convolutions of the iron fence. The moon was above, full and radiant; vehicles and pedestrians were few; sparrows twittered sleepily in the eaves or a little while the scene might have been a country churchyard. And the anthem that the organist played cemented Soapy to the iron fence, for he had known it well in the days when his life contained such things as mothers and roses and ambitions and friends and immaculate thoughts and collars. The conjunction of Soapy’s receptive state of mind and the influences about the old church brought a sudden and wonderful change in his soul. He viewed with rising horror the pit into which he had tumbled, the degraded days, unworthy desires, dead hopes, wrecked faculties and base motives that made up his existence. And also in a moment his heart responded thrillingly to this strange mood. A strong impulse moved him to battle with his desperate fact. He would pull himself out of the mire and would make a man of himself again; he would conquer the evil that had enslaved him. There was time; he was young yet; he would resurrect his old eager ambitions and pursue them without faltering. Those solemn but sweet organ notes had set up a revolution in him. Tomorrow he would go into the roaring downtown district and find work. A fur importer had once offered him a place as driver. He would be somebody in the world. He would..... Soapy felt a hand laid-on arm. He looked quickly around into the impassive face of a policeman. “What are you doin’ here?” asked the officer. “Nothin’,” said Soapy. “Then come along,” said the policeman. “Three months on the island,” said the Magistrate in the Police Court the next morning. Read the extract and complete the activities given below:

     Family can be classified into two types: joint family and nuclear family.

     In the joint family along with parents and children other members like grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, etc. are included. In such family, socialization of children is quicker. Tasks are shared. Responsibilities are shared.

     Establishment of emotional bonds are common leading to mental security. Members learn adjustment. But sometimes there are conflicts and misunderstandings among family members. Children do not get complete attention from their parents.

     On the contrary nuclear family consists of parents and their children. So we see flexibility in parental roles. Parents share their responsibilities. Parent child relationships are very intimate, Full attention is paid on children's personality development. But children lack in making adjustments. Children get too much attention from their parents and so they become demanding and selfish.

     Parenting styles do influence children's behaviour. The best known research on parenting style is Diana Baumrind’s early studies of pre-school children and their parents. She proposed three parenting styles: permissive, authoritarian and authoritative.

     Permissive parents are inconsistent in their behaviour. So children of such parents become dependent, immature.

     Authoritarian parents are rigid and punitive in nature. Children of such parents become unfriendly, unsocial and uninvolved. Parents provide food and shelter to their children but they neglect them and become emotionally detached. That leads to indifferent, rejecting behaviour on the part of the children.

     Authoritative parents encourage independency, they set limits and goals, they are firm in their behaviour. This kind of parenting style makes children self-reliable, independent and develop social skills.

questions.prompt_text: Write a ‘Summary’ ofthe above extract by using the following points - [Types of families - role of the parents - development of personality - socialization of behaviour]
questions.prompt_html:
Write a ‘Summary’ ofthe above extract by using the following points -

[Types of families - role of the parents - development of personality - socialization of behaviour]
questions.solution_html:
Families can be classified into two types: joint families and nuclear families. In a joint family, children live with their parents and other relatives, which facilitates faster socialization and the sharing of responsibilities. Emotional bonds are strong, though conflicts may sometimes arise. In a nuclear family, parents and children live together, and parents play a major role in shaping their children’s personalities by providing them with full attention.

Parenting styles greatly influence the development of a child’s personality and social behaviour. Permissive and authoritarian parenting may negatively affect children, making them dependent or emotionally detached. However, authoritative parenting encourages independence, self-reliance and good social skills. Thus, family and parents play a vital role in the overall development and socialization of a child.

questions.prompt_text: Read the extract and write the appreciation of the poem: Weavers, weaving at break of day, Why do you weave a garment so gay?..... Blue as the wing of a halcyon wild, We weave the robes of a new-born child Weavers, weaving at fall of night, Why do you weave a garment so bright?..... Like the plumes of a peacock, purple and green. We weave the marriage veils of a queen. Weavers, weaving solemn and still, What do you weave in the moonlight chill..... White as a feather and white as a cloud, We weave a dead man’s funeral shroud.
questions.prompt_html:
Read the extract and write the appreciation of the poem:

Weavers, weaving at break of day,
Why do you weave a garment so gay?.....
Blue as the wing of a halcyon wild,
We weave the robes of a new-born child

Weavers, weaving at fall of night,
Why do you weave a garment so bright?.....
Like the plumes of a peacock, purple and green.
We weave the marriage veils of a queen.

Weavers, weaving solemn and still,
What do you weave in the moonlight chill.....
White as a feather and white as a cloud,
We weave a dead man’s funeral shroud.
questions.solution_html:
The poem “Indian Weavers” is written by Sarojini Naidu. It beautifully describes the three important stages of human life: birth, marriage, and death, through the work of weavers.

The poem has a simple question-and-answer form. In each stanza, the poet asks the weavers what they are weaving, and they reply. The garments they weave symbolise different stages of life: a bright blue robe for a newborn child, a colourful marriage veil for a queen, and a white shroud for a dead man. The colours used in the poem are symbolic and meaningful.

The poet has used figures of speech, such as similes, for example, “Blue as the wing of a halcyon wild” and “White as a feather and white as a cloud.” The poem also has a musical quality with rhyme scheme aa bb in each stanza.

The language of the poem is simple, rhythmic and rich in imagery. The poem conveys a profound message: life moves in a cycle from birth to death, and each stage has its own significance. I like the poem for its simplicity and meaningful theme.

questions.prompt_html: Imagine, after your HSC Exam, you wish to pursue a ‘Bachelor’s degree in Performing Arts,’ with Classical Vocal Music in a reputed university in India or abroad. Prepare a ‘Statement of Purpose’ (SOP), in about 150 words which will help you to secure an admission in your dream university.
questions.solution_html:
Music has been an integral part of my life since childhood. After completing my HSC examination, I aspire to pursue a Bachelor’s degree in Performing Arts with a specialization in Classical Vocal Music from a reputed university. My training in classical music for the past few years has nurtured discipline, dedication, and deep respect for our rich musical heritage. Regular performances in school programmes and local competitions have strengthened my confidence and stage presence.

I wish to refine my technical skills, deepen my understanding of ragas and rhythm, and explore the theoretical aspects of Indian classical music under expert guidance. My goal is not only to become a skilled performer but also to help preserve and promote classical music globally. I am hardworking, sincere, and eager to learn. I believe that admission to your esteemed university will provide me with the right platform to grow artistically and academically, and to fulfil my dream of excelling in Classical Vocal Music.

questions.solution_html:
Making Vacation Meaningful

Good morning respected judges, teachers and my dear friends,

Vacation is often seen as a time to relax, travel, and take a break from routine. While rest is important, vacations can also be a golden opportunity for personal growth. A meaningful vacation is not about how far we travel, but how much we learn and experience.

We can use this time to develop new skills, such as learning a language, reading inspiring books, volunteering for social causes, or taking on internships. Spending quality time with family, reconnecting with nature, and focusing on physical and mental well-being also make vacations valuable.

Instead of wasting hours on screens, we should invest time in activities that shape our future and build our character. A meaningful vacation refreshes not just our bodies but also our minds and souls.

Let us make every vacation a step towards becoming better, wiser, and more responsible individuals.

Thank you.

questions.prompt_text: Expand the following idea with the help of the points given below (150 words): ‘Self discipline is self-caring’ Essential qualities: Persistence/determination Perseverance/hard work Devotion/commitment Focus/target/goal Self learning
questions.prompt_html:
Expand the following idea with the help of the points given below (150 words):

‘Self discipline is self-caring’ 

Essential qualities:

  1. Persistence/determination
  2. Perseverance/hard work
  3. Devotion/commitment
  4. Focus/target/goal
  5. Self learning
questions.solution_html:
Self Discipline is Self-Caring

Self-discipline means controlling our actions and emotions to achieve our goals. It is truly a form of self-caring because it helps us grow, improve, and protect our future. When we practice persistence and determination, we do not give up easily. We keep trying even when things become difficult. This builds inner strength and confidence.

Perseverance and hard work are also important qualities of self-discipline. Success does not come overnight; it requires continuous effort and patience. Devotion and commitment towards our work or studies show that we value our responsibilities and respect our dreams.

Having a clear focus and a definite target helps us stay on the right path. Self-discipline prevents distractions and keeps us dedicated to our goals. Self-learning is another key aspect. A disciplined person always tries to learn new things and improve skills.

Thus, self-discipline is self-caring because it shapes our character and leads us toward success and a better life.

questions.solution_html:
Proper Study Habits

Proper study habits play a very important role in a student’s life. They help us understand subjects clearly and perform better in examinations. Good study habits are not about studying for long hours, but about studying with focus and regularity.

Self-discipline is the foundation of effective learning. Avoiding distractions like mobile phones and social media helps us concentrate better. Planning and organisation are equally important. Making a timetable, setting daily goals, and revising regularly make studies easier and less stressful.

In today’s digital world, smartphones have become an inseparable part of our lives. While they are useful for communication and learning, excessive engagement leads to addiction, distraction, and loss of valuable time. Continuous screen time affects our eyesight, disturbs sleep, and reduces physical activity. It also impacts our concentration and mental peace.

It is time to shift from smart phones to smart habits. Let us cultivate good habits like reading books, exercising regularly, spending time with family, and pursuing hobbies such as music, sports, or art. Engaging in meaningful activities keeps our mind active and our body healthy.

You will have to keep learning for the rest of your life because we are now entering an era of lifelong learning,” he said. questions.solution_html:
Impact of Technology on Learning and Jobs

The rapid advancement of disruptive technologies is reshaping industries, shifting the focus from enterprises to consumers. Companies like Facebook, Google, Amazon, and Apple dominate due to the growing influence of consumer technology. This rapid transformation necessitates constant learning and relearning to keep pace with technological changes. Lifelong learning is essential in an era where traditional education alone is insufficient. Instead of formal, long-term academic programs, individuals must engage in short bursts of learning, often through online platforms.

The impact on jobs is significant as automation, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Deep Learning continue to evolve. Many repetitive jobs have already been replaced by technology, and new advancements, such as neural networks, are making machines smarter. The unpredictable nature of future job roles highlights the urgent need for adaptability and continuous skill development.

questions.prompt_text: Read the extract and write the appreciation of the poem given below: Is anybody happier because you passed his way? Does anyone remember that you spoke to him today? This day is almost over, and its toiling time is through; Is there anyone to utter now a kindly word of you? Did you give a cheerful greeting to the friend who came along? Or a churlish sort of “Howdy” and then vanish in the throng? Were you selfish pure and simple as you rushed along the way, Or is someone mighty grateful for a deed you did today? Can you say tonight, in parting with the days that’s slipping fast, That you helped a single brother of the many that you passed? questions.prompt_html:
Read the extract and write the appreciation of the poem given below: 

Is anybody happier because you passed his way?
Does anyone remember that you spoke to him today?
This day is almost over, and its toiling time is through;
Is there anyone to utter now a kindly word of you?

Did you give a cheerful greeting to the friend who came along?
Or a churlish sort of “Howdy” and then vanish in the throng?
Were you selfish pure and simple as you rushed along the way,
Or is someone mighty grateful for a deed you did today?

Can you say tonight, in parting with the days that’s slipping fast,
That you helped a single brother of the many that you passed?
Is a single heart rejoicing over what you did or said;
Does a man whose hopes were fading now with courage look ahead?
questions.solution_html:
1. Title: “Have You Earned Your Tomorrow” 
  2. Poet: Edgar Albert Guest
  3. Theme and Central Idea: The poem emphasizes the importance of kindness, selflessness, and making a positive impact on others' lives. It questions whether we have brought happiness to someone, offered words of encouragement, or performed a good deed during the day. The poem urges us to reflect on our actions and consider how we can make the world a better place by helping others.
  4. Poetic Devices and Style:
    • The poem uses interrogation (rhetorical questions) to encourage self-reflection.
    • Alliteration is used (e.g., “single heart rejoicing”).
    • The poem follows a simple, rhythmic structure, making it easy to read and understand.
  5. Message/Moral: The poem conveys the message that true happiness lies in spreading joy and kindness. It encourages readers to be compassionate, helpful, and considerate towards others, as even small acts of kindness can make a big difference.
  6. My Opinion: I find this poem inspiring and thought-provoking. It reminds us to be kind, helpful, and mindful of our actions. The poem teaches a valuable lesson about the impact of good deeds and encourages us to be better human beings.

Appreciation of the Poem

The poem makes the reader reflect on the importance of kindness and good deeds in daily life. It asks meaningful questions to make us think about whether our actions have made anyone happier or more hopeful. The poet emphasizes that even small acts, like a cheerful greeting or a kind word, can have a big impact on others.

The theme of the poem is human values, kindness, and self-introspection. The poet uses simple language and a question–answer style to directly address the reader. This makes the poem thoughtful and effective.

The poem conveys a strong moral message that our life becomes meaningful only when we help others. It encourages us to be considerate, helpful, and compassionate. The poem inspires readers to reflect on their actions at the end of the day and strive to make a positive difference in the lives of others.

questions.solution_html:
Soldiers and Farmers: The Real Heroes

Good morning, respected judges, teachers, and my dear friends.

It is an honor to stand before you and speak on the topic “Soldiers and Farmers: The Real Heroes”. In today’s world, we often celebrate celebrities and influencers, but the true heroes of our nation are the ones who protect us and feed us our soldiers and farmers.

Soldiers dedicate their lives to safeguarding our borders. Whether it is freezing cold in the mountains or scorching heat in the deserts, they stand strong, ensuring that we live in peace. They leave behind their families so that we can stay safe with ours. Their courage, discipline, and sacrifice are beyond words.

On the other hand, farmers are the lifeline of our country. From sunrise to sunset, they work tirelessly in the fields, growing the food that sustains us. Despite facing unpredictable weather, financial struggles, and hardships, they never stop feeding the nation.

Both soldiers and farmers make enormous sacrifices, often without receiving the recognition they deserve. Without our soldiers, we would have no security; without our farmers, we would have no food. They are the true pillars of our nation.

Let us respect and support these real heroes, for they are the ones who truly shape our future.

Thank you!

questions.prompt_text: Expand the following idea with the help of the points given below (100/150 words). ‘Fortune Favours the Brave’ Stepping out of comfort zone Calculated risks Overcoming fears Mental toughness Building confidence
questions.prompt_html:
Expand the following idea with the help of the points given below (100/150 words).

‘Fortune Favours the Brave’

  • Stepping out of comfort zone
  • Calculated risks
  • Overcoming fears
  • Mental toughness
  • Building confidence
questions.solution_html:
‘Fortune Favours the Brave’

Success and progress belong to those who dare to step out of their comfort zone. Growth happens when people embrace challenges and explore new opportunities instead of staying in their safe space.

Taking calculated risks is another important factor in achieving success. Those who analyze situations, weigh the pros and cons, and take well-thought-out steps are more likely to succeed. Fear often prevents people from moving forward, but overcoming fears is essential for personal and professional growth. Facing difficulties head-on makes a person stronger and more resilient.

Mental toughness plays a significant role in handling setbacks. Strong-minded individuals do not give up in the face of obstacles; instead, they persist and adapt. As a result, they start building confidence, which empowers them to take on even bigger challenges in life.

History has shown that only those who display courage and determination achieve great things. Indeed, fortune always favors the brave.

Title: Sky Force

Personal Impressions: "Sky Force" stands out for its meticulous portrayal of historical events and the Indian Air Force's heroism. The film successfully balances action with emotional narratives, making it a must-watch for those interested in India's military history.

  • Reduces pollution
  • Reduces electricity bills
  • Subsidy by government
questions.solution_html:
Solar Energy: A Sustainable Future

Solar energy is one of the most efficient and eco-friendly sources of power. It is a renewable source of energy, meaning it never runs out and is available abundantly from the sun. By using solar panels, we can harness this energy to generate electricity.

One of the biggest advantages of solar energy is that it helps in reducing pollution. Unlike fossil fuels, it does not release harmful gases into the environment, making it a clean and green energy source. Additionally, installing solar panels can significantly reduce electricity bills. Once installed, they generate free electricity for years, making it a cost-effective solution in the long run.

To encourage the use of solar energy, the government provides subsidies and incentives, making it more affordable for households and businesses. Switching to solar power is a smart choice for a sustainable and energy-efficient future.

questions.prompt_text: Prepare an ‘Appeal' on the topic ‘Women's Security and Safety’ with the help of the following points (100/150 words): Respect women's rights Safety measures and support systems Collective responsibility Government initiatives

questions.solution_html:
Women's Security and Safety - A Shared Responsibility

Women's security and safety are fundamental rights that must be respected by all. Every woman deserves to live without fear and enjoy equal opportunities in society. It is essential to respect women's rights and ensure their dignity at all times.

To enhance women's safety, strong measures such as self-defense training, emergency helplines, and secure public spaces must be implemented. Support systems like women’s helplines and legal aid should be easily accessible to those in need.

Ensuring women's safety is a collective responsibility. Families, communities, and workplaces must foster a culture of respect and zero tolerance for violence or harassment.

The government has introduced various initiatives like women’s helplines (1091), stricter laws, and awareness campaigns to promote safety. However, real change can only happen when society works together to create a safe and empowering environment for women.

Let’s join hands to build a secure and equal world for all women!

questions.solution_html:
“Have You Earned Your Tomorrow” by Edgar Guest is an insightful poem. The title alone raises the question of whether we accomplished anything worthwhile today. It exhorts the reader to consider the individuals in their daily lives. 

The poem’s obvious message is that a person’s life can only be worthwhile if it benefits mankind as a whole. According to the poet, a person’s conscience must recognise that their existence is legitimate. Otherwise, he or she won’t feel entitled to request an additional day of life. 

“Interrogation” is a significant figure of speech. Alliteration and antithesis are also present. Each of the poem’s four stanzas contains four lines. Aabb is the rhyming scheme. The poem has an uplifting tone. 

Readers are forced to examine how they live through interrogation. The language is straightforward, upbeat, and straightforward. I think it’s positive poetry. We may take the lesson and start applying it to our daily lives right away.

Honorable Principal, respected teachers, and my dear friends,

Good morning to all. Today, I stand before you to speak on a topic that is close to my heart: “Travelling is the best experience.”

While books can give us knowledge and classrooms can provide information, it is travel that truly grants us wisdom. When we step out of our comfort zones and explore new places, we don't just see new landscapes; we gain new perspectives. Travelling teaches us things that no textbook ever could: adaptability, patience, and cultural empathy.

Whether it is trekking through the silent mountains or navigating the bustling streets of a historic city, every journey is a lesson in geography, history, and sociology combined.   • Creates conflict

questions.solution_html:
The Worst Kind of Communication

Communication is the bridge that connects hearts and minds, but when it turns into an argument, that bridge collapses. It is often said that “Argument is the worst kind of communication” because it shifts the focus from finding a solution to simply winning a battle of words.

Arguments directly contradict the real values of life, such as empathy, patience, and mutual respect. Instead of fostering understanding, an argument creates conflict and leaves deep emotional scars between friends, family, or colleagues. It becomes a breeding ground for hostility, spreading negativity and souring the overall atmosphere of a home or workplace.

Furthermore, arguing is a colossal waste of time and energy. While a healthy discussion leads to growth, an argument revolves around ego and repetitive points that yield no constructive outcome. To maintain peace and harmony, we must learn to disagree gracefully. Choosing silence or calm dialogue over a heated argument is always a sign of strength and maturity.

This Oscar-winning documentary follows an indigenous couple, Bomman and Bellie, in the Mudumalai Tiger Reserve in India. The heart of the story is their journey of raising Raghu, an orphaned baby elephant. It is not just a film about animal rescue; it is a moving portrayal of the deep, familial bond between humans and nature.

The cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the lush, raw beauty of the Indian wilderness. Every frame feels like a painting. The background score is subtle and soulful, perfectly complementing the tranquil yet emotional moments between the couple and their elephant “child.” The documentary relies on authentic visuals rather than loud narration, making it an immersive experience.

questions.solution_html:
Essentials of a Sustainable Diet Plan

In our fast-paced lives, fitness often takes a backseat. However, a structured diet is not about deprivation; it’s about fueling your body correctly. Here are the essentials of a successful diet plan.

A balanced diet must include a variety of dietary contents. Focus on whole foods: lean proteins, healthy fats, complex carbohydrates, and plenty of fibrous vegetables. Avoid processed sugars and prioritise hydration.

Your diet schedule is as important as what you eat. Instead of heavy, infrequent meals, aim for smaller, balanced portions throughout the day to keep your metabolism active.

The hardest part is sticking to the plan. Cravings are natural, but discipline is what builds long-term habits. Prepare your meals in advance to avoid the temptation of fast food.

Finally, measuring results is vital. Keep a food journal or use an app to track your progress. Listen to your body’s feedback if you feel sluggish; adjust your nutrients. Remember, a diet plan is a marathon, not a sprint!

questions.solution_html:
The Power of Tolerance in Rebuilding Civilization

The extract emphasizes the powerful role of love in private life as the greatest force, yet it points out its limitations in public affairs, citing historical attempts like the Middle Ages and the French Revolution that aimed to apply love in broader societal contexts but ultimately failed. The notion that individuals or entities across vast distances and different spheres should love each other is criticized as unrealistic and ineffective. Instead, the text advocates for tolerance as the essential, albeit less glamorous, virtue necessary for rebuilding civilization post-war. Tolerance, described as the ability to endure and coexist with others, even if they are not personally known or liked, is posited as the foundation on which a civilized future can be constructed. This quality, though dull and negative in its passivity, is deemed crucial for allowing diverse races, classes, and interests to work together toward reconstruction. The summary captures the transition from the impracticality of universal love in public life to the pragmatic embrace of tolerance as the key to a harmonious post-war society.

It is the Inchcape Rock!' Sir Ralph the Rover tore his hair; He curst himself in his despair; The waves rush in every side, The ship is sinking beneath the tide. But even in his dying fear One dreadful sound could the Rover hear, A sound as if with the Incheape Bell, The Devil below was ringing his knell.
questions.prompt_html:
Appreciation:

Read the extract and Write the appreciation of the poem:

They hear no sound, the swell is strong;
Though the wind hath fallen, they drift along,
Till the vessel strikes with a shivering shock,-
O Christ! It is the Inchcape Rock!'

Sir Ralph the Rover tore his hair;
He curst himself in his despair;
The waves rush in every side,
The ship is sinking beneath the tide.

But even in his dying fear
One dreadful sound could the Rover hear,
A sound as if with the Incheape Bell,
The Devil below was ringing his knell.
questions.solution_html:
The given extract from the poem vividly captures the horror and despair of a seafaring tragedy. The poem’s rhythm and rhyme scheme (ABAB) contribute to the building of tension and a sense of foreboding. The use of onomatopoeia in "shivering shock" effectively conveys the violence of the ship striking the rock, while the invocation "O Christ!" underscores the gravity of the situation, blending the religious with the dire immediacy of the moment.

Sir Ralph the Rover's actions of tearing his hair and cursing himself are expressions of extreme remorse and desperation, which are powerful human emotions. The poet’s use of vivid imagery, as the waves rush in and the ship sinks, creates a strong visual impact, placing the reader in the midst of the chaotic and hopeless struggle against nature's fury.

The poem concludes with a chilling auditory image: the sound of the Inchcape Bell tolling not for guidance, but as a death knell, rung by the devil himself. This personification of the bell as an instrument of the devil emphasizes the idea of divine justice and retribution, suggesting that Sir Ralph's actions have led to a fittingly ominous end.

The beauty of this poem lies in its moral message, encapsulated in the dramatic narrative and rich, evocative language that stirs the imagination and evokes deep emotional responses. It serves as a cautionary tale about the consequences of one's actions and the inexorable nature of justice. The haunting ending leaves a lasting impression, making it an exemplary piece of narrative poetry.

Green Revolution

Ladies and gentlemen, today I stand before you to shed light on an initiative that reshaped global agriculture: the Green Revolution. This groundbreaking movement, initiated in the mid-20th century, was pivotal in enhancing food production to combat hunger worldwide. By introducing high-yield crop varieties, advanced irrigation practices, and chemical fertilizers and pesticides, the Green Revolution marked a significant triumph over food scarcity in numerous regions.

However, as we applaud these achievements, it's imperative to acknowledge the associated environmental and social repercussions. The heavy reliance on chemical inputs has led to soil degradation, water shortages, and a decline in biodiversity. Furthermore, the disparity between large-scale and smallholder farmers has intensified, raising concerns about the equity and sustainability of agricultural advancements.

As we contemplate the path ahead, our goal should be to cultivate an agricultural model that embraces increased production without compromising ecological health. A balanced, eco-friendly approach is crucial for ensuring food security and environmental sustainability in harmony.

In conclusion, I wish to express my profound gratitude to all of you for engaging with this vital issue. Your presence here today signifies a collective commitment to nurturing an agricultural future that is both productive and sustainable. Thank you, everyone, for your time and for joining this important dialogue. Together, we can pave the way for a truly green revolution.

questions.solution_html:
Manners Maketh Man

The phrase "Manners Maketh Man" teaches us a powerful lesson: our true self is not just about the actions we take but also about how we carry out those actions. At the heart of displaying good manners is the idea of being polite. Politeness is not just about the words we choose; it also includes our tone of voice, our body language, and our behavior toward others.

Being polite means using words that are kind and thoughtful, speaking in a way that's gentle and friendly, and ensuring our body language is open and welcoming. It's about making sure our actions don't hurt or offend anyone and that we make those around us feel valued and included.

To truly embody these principles, we need to be courteous and amiable. This means always acting with kindness and respect, and treating people well no matter the situation. It's about being a positive presence in the lives of those we interact with, offering a smile or a helpful hand whenever we can.

By focusing on our speech, tone, gestures, and actions in this way, we not only show respect for others but also shape our character in the best possible light. The concept of "Manners Maketh Man" reminds us that being polite and friendly isn't old-fashioned-it's essential. It makes us better individuals and improves the world around us, one respectful interaction at a time.

questions.prompt_text: Give a brief character-sketch of The Narrator.
questions.prompt_html: Give a brief character-sketch of The Narrator.
questions.solution_html:
The narrator of the novel is the author, E.R. Braithwaite, himself. The novel is based on his real-life experiences, which particularly focuses on his life in England and his job as a teacher at Greenslade School after the Second World War. Before becoming a teacher, he worked as an engineer and even served in the Royal British Air Force during the war.
Though he is British, he is a victim of racial discrimination and prejudice because he is a black man in post-war England. Because of his race, he has trouble finding employment and reluctantly takes up the post of a teacher at Greenslade School, located in the East End of London. The school is famous for its badly behaved students and from the first day, Braithwaite finds it difficult to manage his class full of unruly children. As someone who is easily angered, Braithwaite struggles to keep calm while dealing with them. Despite not a teacher by profession, Braithwaite is very insightful in his interactions with the students. He recognizes that he lacks the experience of a professional teacher and takes extra effort to improve his teaching skills. He soon learns to be patient and compassionate towards the students and eventually manages to build a strong bond with them based on mutual respect. He even tries to learn about their backgrounds so as to be able to understand the reasons for their behaviour. Braithwaite is firm but caring and brings about an extraordinary transformation in his students. He is the perfect example of a good teacher, as his influence goes way beyond the classroom and he ends up making a huge difference in his students’ lives. He is intelligent and sensitive and shows genuine concern for the well-being of his students. By not giving up on his students, Braithwaite shows resilience and confidence in his abilities and reaps the rewards of his hard work as he watches with pride the young adults that graduate from his class at the end of the year.

E.R. Braithwaite, the narrator of To Sir, With Love, is an educated, intelligent, and compassionate individual. As a Black teacher in a prejudiced society, he faces racial discrimination but remains patient and determined. He transforms unruly students through respect, discipline, and empathy, emphasizing moral values and personal responsibility.

questions.prompt_text: Explain in brief the theme of 'To Sir, With Love'.
questions.prompt_html: Explain in brief the theme of 'To Sir, With Love'.
questions.solution_html:
The primary theme of the novel is the student-teacher relationship. When Braithwaite first accepts his job as a teacher at Greenslade School, he is met with a bunch of arrogant, disrespectful and illmannered students who were well-known for their bad behaviour. Though angry and frustrated at first, Braithwaite eventually learns to be patient and tolerant towards their antics and develops a strong bond with each of them. Braithwaite is not only concerned with their academic progress but also takes a keen interest in their development as individuals. He even takes the time to find out more about their backgrounds and tries to understand the reasons for their behaviour. More importantly, he builds a relationship with the students, which is based on mutual respect. Braithwaite addresses the girls as ‘Miss’ and the boys by their last name and in turn asks the students to refer to him as ‘Sir’, relaying the message that a healthy student-teacher relationship is one which involves both, give and take. Though this method is initially resisted by the students, they eventually warm up to it. This can be clearly seen when Braithwaite expresses his appreciation of Denham addressing the senior girls as ‘Miss’. The extract highlights the importance of a teacher’s role in the lives of his/her students. Braithwaite’s influence extends far beyond his academic role. By choosing not to give up on his students, Braithwaite sets an example for how a teacher should be someone who is tolerant and understanding. Through Braithwaite’s role in shaping the personalities of his students, the extract demonstrates that a teacher’s work is not merely limited to the classroom. An important aspect of the student-teacher relationship is also the freedom to be honest. Braithwaite encourages his students to be honest and fearless, which is clearly demonstrated in Denham’s respectful but blunt criticism of the P.T. class, thus conveying the idea that students must be active participants in their own progress. His method of developing a relationship based on mutual respect is effective and results in the transformation of his students from mischievous children to young adults. Braithwaite witnesses this transformation with pride as he watches his students present the class report and admires them for the progress that they have made.

The relationship between a teacher and student, as well as the student council's biannual report, are the themes of "To Sir, With Love." It shows how the behaviour of the children has improved and how confident they are becoming. The contact between students and teachers is also shown to be free.

As I was growing up, I witnessed forests being cleared and replaced by commercial plantations, which destroyed local biodiversity and the capacity of the forests to conserve water. Throughout Africa, women are the primary caretakers, holding significant responsibility for tilling the land and feeding their families. As a result, they are often the first to become aware of environmental damage as resources become scarce and they are incapable of sustaining their families. The women we worked with recounted that, unlike in the past, they were unable to meet their basic needs. But international trade controlled the price of the exports from these small-scale farmers, and a reasonable and just income could not be guaranteed. I came to understand that when the environment is destroyed, plundered or mismanaged, we undermine the quality of our life and that of future generations. Tree planting became a natural choice to address some of the initial basic needs identified by women. Also, tree planting is simple, attainable and guarantees quick, successful results within a reasonable amount of time. This sustains interest and commitment. Together, we have planted over 30 million trees that provide fuel, food, shelter, and income to support our children’s education and household needs. The activity also creates employment and improves soil and watersheds. Initially, the work was difficult because they were unaware that a degraded environment leads to a scramble for scarce resources and may culminate in poverty and even conflict. They were also unaware of the injustices of international economic arrangements. Later, they became aware of the widespread destruction of the ecosystems, especially through deforestation, climatic instability and contamination of the soil and waters - all contributed to excruciating poverty and subsequent riots. questions.solution_html:
Impact of Commercial Farming in Africa

Commercial farming has significantly impacted Africa, particularly affecting the women, who traditionally played a key role in agriculture. As large-scale plantations replaced small farms, many women lost their land and livelihood, leading to economic struggles. Environmental disruption and mismanagement have resulted in deforestation, soil degradation, and loss of biodiversity, which, in turn, have worsened food insecurity. While commercial farming has brought economic benefits like increased production and exports, it has also led to social and ecological imbalances, affecting the overall quality of life in the region. Therefore, we must wisely manage the negative effects of plantations, even though they boost the economy.

questions.prompt_html:
Read the extract and write the appreciation of the poem given below:

My father travels on the late evening train
Standing among silent commuters in the yellow light
Suburbs slide past his unseeing eyes
His shirt and pants are soggy and his black raincoat
Stained with mud and his bag stuffed with books
Is falling apart. His eyes dimmed by age
Fade homeward through the humid monsoon night.
Now I can see him getting off the train
Like a word dropped from a long sentence.
He hurries across the length of the grey platform,
Crosses the railway line, enters the lane,
His chappals are sticky with mud, but he hurries onward.
questions.solution_html:
1. Title: Father Returning Home
  2. Poet: Dilip Chitre
  3. About the Poem and Poet: The poem describes a father’s daily struggles as he commutes home after work. The poet highlights his exhaustion, routine, and unnoticed sacrifices through vivid imagery.
  4. Theme: The poem focuses on parental sacrifice, urban life struggles, and emotional disconnect. It portrays how a father tirelessly works for his family but remains unnoticed.
  5. Poetic Devices: 
    • Imagery: “His chappals are sticky with mud” – shows physical exhaustion.
    • Metaphor: “Like a word dropped from a long sentence” – symbolizes insignificance.
    • Personification: “Suburbs slide past his unseeing eyes” – depicts fatigue.
  6. Message and Moral: The poem conveys that parents silently endure hardships for their families. It reminds us to recognize and appreciate their sacrifices before it’s too late.
  7. Personal Opinion: I find the poem touching and relatable, as it beautifully captures a father’s silent dedication. The poet’s simple yet powerful words create a lasting impact.

Statement of Purpose

I am writing to express my ardent desire to pursue a Bachelor’s degree in Communication Skills at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign (UIUC). My passion for communication was ignited while actively participating in school debates, culminating in leading my team to victory at the National High School Debate Championship. This experience, coupled with my fascination with UIUC’s renowned Speech Communication course, solidified my desire to hone my skills under the guidance of esteemed faculty like Professor Jane Smith.

UIUC’s emphasis on practical application through its “Public Speaking Workshop” programme deeply resonates with my learning style. I believe the integration of real-world scenarios with theoretical knowledge will equip me to excel in diverse communication settings and contribute meaningfully to a globalized world.

‘Should we keep pets?’

Respected Judges, Teachers, and My Dear Friends,

Good morning to all! Today, I would like to share my thoughts on a topic that touches many hearts— the bond between humans and their animal companions. Pets have always held a special place in our lives, offering more than just companionship.

Pets are more than just animals; they are companions, stress relievers, and loyal friends. They provide emotional support, reduce loneliness, and teach responsibility. Studies show that owning a pet can improve mental and physical health by reducing stress and encouraging an active lifestyle.

However, keeping pets also comes with responsibilities. They require proper care, time, and attention. Neglecting them can lead to health issues and emotional distress for both the pet and the owner. In conclusion, keeping pets is a wonderful experience if done with love, care, and responsibility. It is essential to treat them as family members, ensuring their well-being.

Thank you!

questions.prompt_text: Read the following proverb. Share your view and expand the ideas. The wise man has long ears and a short tongue!
questions.prompt_html:
Read the following proverb. Share your view and expand the ideas.

The wise man has long ears and a short tongue!
questions.solution_html:
‘The wise man has long ears and a short tongue.’

A wise person listens more and speaks less. One should be a good listener, as it allows them to understand situations better before responding. A short tongue symbolises self-control; one speaks only after careful thought. People who listen patiently grasp the essence of a conversation, while impulsive speakers may miss crucial details.

Listening enhances knowledge, as it helps in learning from others’ experiences. A person who listens attentively absorbs valuable information, processes it, and responds wisely rather than reacting instantly. Wise individuals take time to understand before forming opinions, making their words more impactful.

Speaking to the point catches attention because brief and meaningful words hold more weight than excessive talk. Thoughtful speech ensures clarity and respect in communication.

Thus, wisdom lies in maintaining a balance—listening patiently, learning continuously, and speaking only when necessary. This is why nature has given us two ears but only one mouth, emphasising the importance of listening over speaking.

questions.prompt_text: Sherlock Holmes is the leading character in the extract. Explain.
questions.prompt_html: Sherlock Holmes is the leading character in the extract. Explain.
questions.solution_html:
At the beginning of the extract, we see that Miss Mary Morstan comes to meet Sherlock Holmes with a case. Through her conversation with Holmes, we come to know that in the past he had solved a case for Miss Morstan’s employer, Mrs. Cecil Forrester. This is the first time we are introduced to Sherlock Holmes as a detective. Dr. Watson describes him as having clear-cut, hawk-like features. Upon listening to Miss Morstan’s story, he is the one who questions her further. This helps the reader understand Holmes’ importance in the extract, thus adding weight to his character. After Miss Morstan leaves, Holmes swings into action by going out to gain more information about the case. Upon his return, he shares his findings with Dr. Watson, which are quite commendable considering he was able to gain so much information in one afternoon. This further strengthens his character as the main lead in the story. An important point of observation is Holmes’ stark refusal to let emotions come in the way of solving a case. This lack of emotion not only sets him apart from Watson, but also from the average reader, making him an extraordinary character. It is perhaps this complete focus on rationality and logic that enables Holmes to make quick advances in the case. On the carriage ride, Holmes deciphers the contents of the page that Miss Morstan shares with him, thus highlighting his intellectual prowess. On the second carriage ride, as the trio are being taken away to an unknown destination, Dr. Watson feels lost, but Holmes is able to clearly identify the places through which the carriage passes. Holmes is, therefore, depicted as the leading character in the extract through the qualities exhibited by him over the course of the story.

‘The Sign of Four’ is a detective fiction with Sherlock Holmes as the main character. He consistently applies the correct deduction theory when solving cases. Holmes is praised for his ability to decipher the handwriting in Mary’s letter. Holmes is portrayed as bright, accurate, clever, and meticulous, with a strong track record of solving cases. He is eager to ask questions and offer assistance. He maintains clear judgement while working on the issue, avoiding emotional distractions.

Write the poetic appreciation of the extract given below:

She walks in beauty, like the night
Of cloudless climes and starry skies;
And all that’s best of dark and bright

Meet in her aspect and her eyes;
Thus mellowed to that tender light
Which heaven to gaudy day denies.

One shade the more, one ray the less,
Had half impaired the nameless grace
Which waves in every raven tress,
Or softly lightens o’er her face;

questions.solution_html:
Appreciation of the poem
‘She Walks in Beauty’

  1. About the poem/poet and the title:
    The poem, 'She Walks in Beauty’ is a poem appreciating female beauty and expressing how outer beauty stems from inner beauty, thus resulting in perfection through harmony. It was written by George, Gordon Byron, well-known as Lord Byron, who was a famous poet from the Romantic era of English literature. At the age of 21, he started a tour of Europe and the Orient (East) after which he composed ‘Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage’ which made him very popular in England.
  2. The Theme:
    The title ‘She walks in beauty’ doesn’t mean that the woman is walking beautifully or that she is simply beautiful. It says that she walks “in beauty”, meaning that beauty surrounds her, making her magnificent.
    In this poem, the primary theme explored by the poet is that of beauty, where he praises a woman he encounters as being flawless. The other themes are that of the delicate harmony between darkness and light as well as the perfect balance between the mind and the body, which makes the woman beautiful even on the inside. 
  3. Poetic style:
    The poem follows a regular rhyme scheme of ‘abab’ throughout. The language used by the poet is rich and complex, which gives the woman in the poem a very mystical quality. The use of a variety of poetic devices like Alliteration, Antithesis, Consonance, Exclamation, Inversion, Metaphor, Metonymy, Personification, Repetition, and Synecdoche add to the complexity of the poem.
  4. The language/poetic devices used in the poem:
    The poet has employed literary devices like enjambment and imagery to enhance its appeal. The visual imagery can be witnessed when the poet compares the woman to a cloudless and starry night, thus laying the foundation of the light and dark theme of the poem.
  5. Special features:
    The qualities attributed to the woman’s features ‘mellowed eyes’, ‘wavy raven tresses’, ‘soft and calm face’ paint a beautiful picture of an extraordinarily wonderful woman. The main symbolism in the poem is that the poet presents the woman as someone who is a symbol of purity and innocence.
  6. Message, values, morals in the poem:
    The message that the poet is trying to convey through this poem is that one can be beautiful on the outside only when one feels beautiful on the inside. Though this poem is largely about the poet trying to capture this woman’s paradoxical beauty, which combines the best of dark and bright, the last stanza focuses on how her stunning appearance stems from her calm, composed mind, and sweet, innocent heart. It is her virtuous nature that gives her beauty that is unparalleled.
  7. Your opinion about the poem:
    In my opinion, the poem is full of class and elegance. The poet’s depiction of the woman’s attractiveness and his expression of the woman’s outer beauty being linked to her inner beauty, create a powerful impact on the readers’ minds, thus making them understand the absolute meaning of being beautiful.

Welcoming the guests -

Welcome to this amazing evening, ladies and gentlemen, distinguished guests, professors, parents, and most importantly, our dear kids. We are gathered here to say goodbye to our incredible group of H.S.C. examination candidates. This evening is devoted to honouring their efforts, commitment, and successes throughout their academic careers.

Let us begin this important occasion by warmly welcoming all of the distinguished guests who have honoured us with their presence today. We are honoured to have each of you here, as your support and guidance have had a huge impact on the lives of these exceptional people.

questions.prompt_text: Expansion of Idea: Expand the following idea with the help of the points given below (100-150 words) – “Experience is the best teacher” It’s practical and not theoretical experience Learn from situations Direct and first-hand knowledge Real-life versus Bookish

Expand the following idea with the help of the points given below (100-150 words) –

“Experience is the best teacher”

  • It’s practical and not theoretical experience
  • Learn from situations
  • Direct and first-hand knowledge
  • Real-life versus Bookish
questions.solution_html:
“Experience is the best teacher”

‘Experience is the best teacher' is a well-known proverb. It means wisdom is gained through personal experiences. Books are considered to be the source of all knowledge, but all that one learns through a book is only of theoretical nature in the form of ideas and concepts.

We get knowledge by reading books, listening to speeches, talking to people, etc. They provide just theoretical knowledge, but real-life experiences teach us practical or real things. We must learn from real-life situations.

Experience gives us direct and first-hand knowledge. It teaches us how to do better, how to overcome challenges, and how to learn from our mistakes. The worst experience is the best teacher. By visiting historical places, we may learn History. By visiting oceans and forests, we may learn Geography. Such real-life experiences teach us great lessons.

Bookish knowledge is imperfect, whereas real-life experience is perfect. It teaches lifelong lessons. So it is said that - Experience is the best teacher.

questions.prompt_text: Give a brief character-sketch of The Narrator.
questions.prompt_html: Give a brief character-sketch of The Narrator.
questions.solution_html:
The narrator of the novel is the author, E.R. Braithwaite, himself. The novel is based on his real-life experiences, which particularly focuses on his life in England and his job as a teacher at Greenslade School after the Second World War. Before becoming a teacher, he worked as an engineer and even served in the Royal British Air Force during the war.
Though he is British, he is a victim of racial discrimination and prejudice because he is a black man in post-war England. Because of his race, he has trouble finding employment and reluctantly takes up the post of a teacher at Greenslade School, located in the East End of London. The school is famous for its badly behaved students and from the first day, Braithwaite finds it difficult to manage his class full of unruly children. As someone who is easily angered, Braithwaite struggles to keep calm while dealing with them. Despite not a teacher by profession, Braithwaite is very insightful in his interactions with the students. He recognizes that he lacks the experience of a professional teacher and takes extra effort to improve his teaching skills. He soon learns to be patient and compassionate towards the students and eventually manages to build a strong bond with them based on mutual respect. He even tries to learn about their backgrounds so as to be able to understand the reasons for their behaviour. Braithwaite is firm but caring and brings about an extraordinary transformation in his students. He is the perfect example of a good teacher, as his influence goes way beyond the classroom and he ends up making a huge difference in his students’ lives. He is intelligent and sensitive and shows genuine concern for the well-being of his students. By not giving up on his students, Braithwaite shows resilience and confidence in his abilities and reaps the rewards of his hard work as he watches with pride the young adults that graduate from his class at the end of the year.

E.R. Braithwaite, the narrator of To Sir, With Love, is an educated, intelligent, and compassionate individual. As a Black teacher in a prejudiced society, he faces racial discrimination but remains patient and determined. He transforms unruly students through respect, discipline, and empathy, emphasizing moral values and personal responsibility.

questions.prompt_html:
Read the following extract and complete the activities given below:

"This is my birthday, sir," explained Gopal timidly. "Wish you many happy returns," said the director promptly and added, "What if it is your birthday?"

"Rather a peculiar birthday," explained Gopal. "This is my forty-ninth birthday. Astrologers have often told me that I might not see this birthday, and if I lived to see this day I should have nothing more to worry about... I have lived in secret terror of this ‘day all my life. Whenever I saw my wife and children I used to be racked with the thought that I should probably be leaving them orphans. I came late today because we held some propitiatory rites at home for the planets, and we celebrated my survival this day with a feast. My astrologer has suggested that I do nothing unpleasant today, sir. I wish to treat it as a very auspicious day, sir."

The director was impressed. He turned to his assistant, who always shadowed him, carrying a portfolio under his arm and commanded, ‘fetch the story-writer’. Presently he arrived, his lips red with the chewing of betel leaves. He was a successful story-writer who made a lot of money by dashing off plots for film people. He laughed aloud on hearing of the problem created by the actor. He was not the angry type to feel upset at contrary suggestions.

He declared, 'Impossible to change the story. How can he refuse to die? I am busy.

He turned on his heel and started out. At the door he stopped to add, "Anyway, send for our boss and tell him about it." The boss came running into the scene. He asked anxiously, "What is all this trouble about? What is it all about?"

Gopal sat in his chair unmoving: he was not allowed to shift his position even slightly: continuity would be spoilt otherwise. He felt stuffy. The big lamp scorched his face. They all stood around and looked at him as if he were a freak. Their faces were blurred beyond the shadows. 'All of them are my Yamas,' Gopal thought. 'They are bent upon seeing me dead.'

A1. Arrange the following statements in a proper sequence as per their occurrence in the extract and rewrite:

  1. The director was impressed.
  2. Their faces were blurred beyond the shadows.
  3. Gopal explained timidly that it was his birthday.
  4. His lips were red with the chewing of betel leaves.

A2. Give reasons:

  1. Gopal’s forty-ninth birthday was a peculiar one because ....
  2. He felt stuffy because ....

A3. 'All of them are my Yamas'. Explain the statement.

A4. 'Superstitions poison our minds'. Explain in your own words.

A5. Do as directed.

  1. He laughed aloud on hearing of the problem. 
    (Choose the correct change in the given options, if 'would' is used in the above sentence.)
    1. He would laughed on hearing of the problem.
    2. He would have laughed on hearing of the problem.
    3. He would laugh aloud on hearing of the problem.
    4. He would be laughed on hearing of the problem.
  2. They all stood around and looked at him. (Choose the correct alternative to write it with 'not only ... but also ... .')
    1. They all not only stood around but also looked at him.
    2. They all stood not only around but also looked at him.
    3. Not only they all stood around but also looked at him.
    4. They all stood not around only but also looked at him.

A6. Find out the antonyms for the following from the extract:

  1. bravely
  2. pleasant
  3. accept
  4. moving
questions.solution_html:
A1. 

iii. Gopal explained timidly that it was his birthday.

i. The director was impressed.

iv. His lips were red with the chewing of betel leaves.

ii. Their faces were blurred beyond the shadows.

A2. 

  1. Gopal’s forty-ninth birthday was a peculiar one because astrologers predicted that everything would be OK if he lived through this birthday. He, therefore, wished to avoid doing anything unpleasant and treat it as an auspicious day. To his dismay, though, he was supposed to die in the movie he was playing in on that same day. 
  2.  He felt stuffy because he was forced to remain motionless while sitting in a chair. Because of continuity issues, he was unable to move even a little. In addition, his face was burning from the large lamp.

A3. Due to his superstitious beliefs, Gopal feared that he would pass away before reaching his 49th birthday. However, the narrative writer refused to alter the scenario in which he was supposed to die in the movie in which he was acting. The large bulb burned Gopal's face as he sat motionless in a chair when the boss arrived. In this instance, he believed that the individuals before him were "Yamas," or the Gods of Death.

A4. This statement is true. Superstitious beliefs make us fearful of a variety of things. It prevents us from moving forward and from realising our greatest potential. In our journey, it drags us back. We question a lot of things, even our own skills. It is therefore like poison to our brains.

A5. 

  1. He would laugh aloud on hearing of the problem.
  2. They all not only stood around but also looked at him.

A6. 

  1. bravely × timidly
  2. pleasant × unpleasant
  3. accept × refuse
  4. moving × unmoving

questions.prompt_html:
Read the extract and complete the activities given below:

No stir in the air, no stir in the sea,
The ship was as still as she could be,
Her sails from heaven received no motion,
Her keel was steady in the ocean.

Without either sign or sound of their shock
The waves flow'd over Inchcape Rock;
So little they rose, so little they fell,
They did not move the Inchcape Bell.

The Abbot of Aberbrothok
Had placed that bell on the Inchcape Rock;
On a buoy in the storm it floated and swung.
And over the waves its warning rung.

When the Rock was hid by the surge’s swell,
The mariners heard the warning bell;
And then they knew the perilous Rock,
And blest the Abbot of Aberbrothok.

A1. Global Understanding:   (2)

Describe the scene in the beginning of the poem.

A2. Inference/Interpretation/Analysis:   (2)

Give reasons:

  1. The ship was still at sea because...
  2. The Abbot of Aberbrothok had placed the bell on the Inchcape Rock so...

A3. Personal Response:   (2)

Write two incidents/occasions when you helped other people.

A4. Poetic Devices:   (2)

Give the rhyming pairs and rhyme scheme from stanza 2 from the extract. 

A5. Poetic Creativity:   (2)

Compose four lines of your own on 'The Sea'.
questions.solution_html:
A1. In the beginning of the poem, the sea was calm and there was no wind. The ship was still and steady and hardly moved. The waves flowed so gently over the Inchcape Rock that they did not even move the Inchcape Bell. It was a serene and calm scene. 

A2. 

  1. The ship was still at sea because there was no breeze, and the waves were calm and soft.
  2. The Abbot of Aberbrothok had placed the bell on the Inchcape Rock so that it would ring during a storm and alert the seafarers to the hazardous hidden rock that they needed to avoid.

A3. During the lift's repair, I assisted my elderly neighbour in carrying a bulky bag upstairs. Assisting the building's security guard with his young daughter's school admissions paperwork was another task I completed. He couldn't understand the English on the form.

A4. Rhyming pairs: Shock - Rock; fell - Bell.

Rhyme Scheme: aabb

A5. The Sea

The sea, the sea, the mighty sea,
From where do you start and where do you end;
It's always a mystery to me
How so many colours in you do you blend.

questions.prompt_html:
Read the given extract and write a poetic appreciation of the poem with the help of the following points.

When I had money, money, O!
I knew no joy till I went poor;
For many a false man as a friend
Came knocking all day at my door.

Then felt I like a child that holds
A trumpet that he must not blow
Because a man is dead; I dared
Not speak to let this false world know.

Much have I thought of life, and seen
How poor men's hearts are ever light;
And how their wives do hum like bees
About their work from morn till night.

So, when I hear these poor ones laugh,
And see the rich ones coldly frown
Poor men, think I, need not go up
So much as rich men should come down.

When I had money, money, O!
My many friends proved all untrue;
But now I have no money, O!
My friends are real, though very few.
  • About the poet and the title
  • The theme
  • Language/poetic devices used in the poem
  • Inspirational message, values, morals reflected in the poem.
  • Special features
  • Your opinion about the poem
questions.solution_html: The poem 'Money' is written by William H. Davies. It is a reflective poem that deals with the poet’s status as both, a rich and a poor man. Based on his own narrative, the poet has depicted a connection between money and personal happiness. The theme of the poem is the inverse relation between money and happiness since the poet had many false friends during his times of richness and much fewer but real friends when he had become poor. The poet has beautified the poem by employing numerous figures of speech such as alliteration, antithesis, consonance, exclamation, inversion, onomatopoeia, metaphor, metonymy, simile, and repetition. Among the special features of the poem, imagery and enjambment are more prominent. The poet follows a simple, narrative style to convey his thoughts. Through this poem, the poet is trying to spread the message that wealth is not required to be truly happy. I feel happiness lies in having genuine people in life, which makes the poor man truly wealthy; as he might not have monetary wealth or a lot of people in his life, but the ones he does have are true to him, thus making him wealthy in the true sense. The poet has made use of five four lined stanzas with the uniform rhyme scheme of  'a b c d' throughout the poem. He repeats the word 'money' to stress the fact that money is unnecessarily given undue importance by man. He wants to suggest that money cannot bring happiness.

Statement of Purpose

Business is my passion. My parents as well as my grandparents were all businessmen/businesswomen in some form or the other and I can think of no other career except doing business. I literally grew up surrounded by discussions about the starting of various businesses. 

I have interviewed a lot of people and conducted extensive study on the launch of different firms over the past year. I was employed as an intern for a startup electronics company while on vacation.

Attending the "Royal Institute of Management" would be an amazing opportunity for me. I promise to work hard and am sure that I will contribute once I am accepted to your university.

questions.solution_html:
Evaluator: Today, "Save Water — Methods to Conserve Water" is the subject of your group discussion. You have three minutes to consider the subject. All right, you can start the conversation now. Who wants to lead the way?
Shaila: I want to start the conversation. Since rainwater is so essential to living, I believe we must find ways to conserve it.
Arjun: It's true that we must save water. We ought to support rainwater gathering techniques in both urban and rural settings.
Norman: Discussions on this subject should be promoted in schools and colleges. The need to find solutions to conserve fresh water has increased due to the rapidly of severe climate change.
Shaila: Another concept is to recycle wastewater for use in toilet flushing and landscaping. These techniques ought to be required in all towns and cities, in my opinion.
Arjun: Small dams and bunds can be built in rural regions to store rainfall. It is important to remind people to turn off the faucets when not in use. Any leak of any kind needs to be fixed.
Norman: One effective solution is to charge for excess water usage and.........
Evaluator: It's time to wrap up the conversation.
Arjun: We can all agree that there should be appropriate ways to preserve fresh water and that people must be made aware of them. Schools and universities should stress the significance of this. As a last point, I want to remind everyone that "No water, No life."

Annual Prize Distribution Function

– By a Magazine Editor

December 18: The college's Annual Prize Distribution Function, held in the Auditorium today, went off well, much to the relief of student organizers.

As is usual, the function opened with a college prayer. The Chief Guest Commander Bahl, Principal Rao, Dean Shastri, and Student Representative Mythili Patil ignited the lamp. Principal Rao gave an introduction speech, and the Chief Guest spoke briefly about the Navy. This was fascinating. 

The Cultural items that followed were extremely impressive, right from the humorous skit, the traditional and modern fusion dances, to the musicals. The audience, of course, gave full encouragement to the performers with their foot-tapping and applause. The prize winners were also applauded and one and all looked pleased.

The Dean of Students' Affairs gave a vote of appreciation to conclude the event. The image of the Chief Guest surrounded by youngsters excited to serve in the Navy and serve their country will live on in people's memories.

Imagine you have taken part in an ‘Elocution Competition’. You have selected the topic ‘Importance of Science and Technology’. 

Draft a speech in about 150 words that you wish to deliver before the audience.
questions.solution_html:
Respected judges, teachers, and my dear friends, 

Good morning. Today, I, XYZ, would like to share a few thoughts on the "importance of science and technology" in honour of "Science Day."

Science and technology provide many advantages. We use the advantages of science in one way or another from the moment the alarm goes off in the morning until we close our eyes at night. Thanks to modern advancements like the automobile, train, etc., we can go around conveniently. Thanks to research, we can eat well and lead healthy lives. Is it possible for us to envision a world without phones, refrigerators, or electricity? We'd go back to being cavemen!

Our lives are certainly being made easier by science and technology. But there is a drawback as well. Who can forget that science produced the atomic bomb, which wreaked such havoc during World War II? Today's terrorists use science to murder thousands of people. There are drawbacks to both the internet and mobile phones. However, I will conclude that it is up to us humans to accept the benefits and ignore the negative ones. Humanity will only advance at that point since science and technology are here to stay.

Thank you.

questions.prompt_text: Expand the following idea with the help of the points given below (100/150 words): 'Actions speak louder than words' Focus on actions Words are useless where there is no action Actions lead to success/result
questions.prompt_html:
Expand the following idea with the help of the points given below (100/150 words):
'Actions speak louder than words'

  • Focus on actions
  • Words are useless where there is no action
  • Actions lead to success/result
questions.solution_html:
Actions speak louder than words

This is an old and wise saying. A person's actions speak louder than their words, according to the saying. Even if we can't always persuade others with just words, we can persuade them by our actions. Without action, words are nothing. We must thus concentrate on doing action. Especially when working with youngsters, this is crucial. Instead of listening to what their parents say, children naturally imitate their behaviour.

When someone speaks, their words are only audible to the ears; yet, when they act, their actions are visible to the eyes. These have a greater effect on the observer than words do. "You must be the change you wish to see in the world," Mahatma Gandhi once stated.

Unless he changes himself, a lazy father cannot expect his lazy children to get better just by urging them to. He must transform his own conduct in order to become an example. Hence, by changing our own behaviour, we can encourage others to follow suit and contribute to a constructive transformation of society.

questions.solution_html:
Review of the film 'A Wednesday'

This 2008 thriller recounts the events that occur between 2 and 6 p.m. on a Wednesday when a guy convinces the police commissioner that he has planted bombs in key locations throughout Mumbai and is holding the city hostage. Only once specific terrorists serving sentences in Mumbai jails are released and brought to a designated destination will the locations be made public.

Only the background score is included; there are no songs or dances. The police commissioner's office, an airport runway, and the roof of an incomplete building in Mumbai serve as the three primary locations for the movie.

The main characters are Jimmy Shergill and Aamir Bashir as police officers, Anupam Kher as the police commissioner, and Naseeruddin Shah as the mysterious bomber. Each character has done a good job in his role. With his role, Naseeruddin Shah steals the show. His delivery of dialogue is simply amazing. The character is given importance by Anupam Kher, who has done it exceptionally well.

After Mumbai's repeated train bombings, hundreds of innocent people died. "A Wednesday" highlights the common man's powerlessness and rage in addition to raising concerns about the injustice done to him.

A great movie with outstanding performers. Not to be missed.

Personality development is essential in today’s competitive world, as it helps shape a confident and successful individual. It is not just about external appearance, but also about developing positive attitudes, good behavior, and a balanced mindset.

A strong personality is crucial for building self-confidence, improving relationships, and achieving success in both personal and professional life. It helps you stand out and leave a lasting impression.

Effective communication is a vital part of personality development. It enhances your ability to express thoughts clearly, connect with others, and build strong relationships. Good communication skills make you a better leader and listener.

Personality development covers multiple aspects like emotional stability, positive attitude, self-discipline, and time management. It helps you become a better version of yourself.

The way you dress reflects your personality. Dressing appropriately boosts your confidence and creates a positive first impression.

In conclusion, personality development is a continuous journey that helps you grow and succeed in life.

questions.solution_html: Mary comes to meet Sherlock with a case. For the past six years, an anonymous person has been sending a pearl to Mary on the same day each year. However, this year, she has received a letter from the anonymous sender requesting her to go to the third pillar from the left, outside the Lyceum Theatre. The letter suggested that Mary had been wronged in some way and that she shall have justice. Though the sender warned Mary not to inform the police, he did tell her that she could have two friends accompany her. At this point, Mary is curious about the meeting but at the same time, the prospect of meeting a stranger alone is obviously unsettling. This statement is important because Mary’s decision to approach Holmes and his subsequent approval to accompany her lead to the unveiling of the mystery of the anonymous sender and of the bigger, main plot of the novel.

Where you selfish pure and simple as you rushed along the way,
Or is someone mighty grateful for a deed you did today?
Can you say tonight, in imparting with the days that's slipping fast,
That you helped a single brother of the many that you passed?
Is a single heart rejoicing over what you did or said;
Does a man whose hopes were fading now with courage look ahead?

Points:

  1. Title of the poem, name of the poet.
  2. Theme
  3. Poetic devices, language
  4. Values
  5. Your opinion about the poem.
questions.solution_html:
Edgar Guest wrote the poem 'Have You Earned Your Tomorrow?' This poem is divided into four stanzas, which are subdivided into sets of four lines quatrains. All these lines follow the rhyming pattern of aabbccaaddeeffaa.

The repetition of the 'ay' sound, which comes in the first, second, and fourth stanzas, has been employed to bring the text together. As the reader notices the opening, 'Have Non Earned Your Tomorrow,' he also notices that the narrative is characterized with questions aimed at the reader. Each verse comprises at least two, and frequently three, concerns about how one treats others. The poem also asks the reader probing questions about how they spend their days. The poem begins with the speaker asking a reader if they did anything to improve the day of another human being. He continues to ask if the reader has greeted their friends cheerfully or if he has wasted the day if he has left a trait of kindness or a scar of discontent.

The speaker probes the reader's behaviour more in the final two stanzas. Everyone should strive to give to others who lack hope and bravery. The speaker of the poem reminds the reader that God alone determines whether or not there will be a tomorrow. Therefore, if one wishes to see the following day, one should carefully evaluate their activities.
