Teacher: You all have a few minutes to consider your preferences, concentrating on the habit of reading. You may now start the conversation. Who is willing to begin?
Sujit: I would like to begin by saying that I actually like outdoor games like cricket, football, volleyball, etc. At first, I considered reading to be a rather tedious and monotonous habit. To understand it fully, you must read it while spending a lot of time alone. I used to prefer to avoid reading, but after reading Lal King to my parents and older brother, I've come to appreciate how reading benefits us in a variety of ways by providing a window into the world. I now make it a point to avoid becoming too involved before reading things.
I: Sujit, I completely agree with you, albeit I'm not sure I understand what you're saying. I read several novels that my sister gave to me as a present, and I've since fallen in love with reading. Reading is unquestionably a beneficial habit. We may also use the internal because there are hundreds of books about it. Audiobooks also assist us in hearing the narrative.
Rohit: I'll admit that I disagree partially since for me, working for hours in front of a computer or while wearing a mobile device is tiresome. Instead, I would like to grab a book, unwind in a chair, and continue reading for hours. Reading takes strong tenacity and patience to fully comprehend everything. It gives us the chance to encounter various characters, situations, and reactions to those experiences.
Kishor: Listening to all of this makes me extremely happy. I also enjoy watching television and playing video or computer games. However, my mother assisted me in developing a reading habit, and reading has now become my favourite activity. Now I understand that reading exposes us to a variety of situations, some of which are extremely difficult, and teaches us how to deal with and overcome them. It forces us to look within ourselves, understand, and objectively analyze our reactions.
Teacher: Now I feel that it is time to reach the conclusion.
Sujit: In conclusion, I believe that everyone of us has unique interests, hobbies, and loves and dislikes. But everyone has come to understand the value of reading in our life. We must continue reading consistently if we want to improve our knowledge.

Ambahogai, October 26th

- by Rajiv Mukherji.

The NSS unit of Vivekanand College, Ambajogai organised a camp at Phavadewadi village. It held from 21st to 24th October. Our group leaders had already visited the village and made contact with the local authorities and elders. There were 72 volunteers in the camp. They were assigned various tasks. There, we had assessed the needs of the community and gathered supplies including medications, books, stationery, seeds, and saplings in accordance with those needs. We were housed at the village's school building. The locals were quite welcoming since they understood who we were. We taught them about topics like agricultural rotation, sanitation, and personal cleanliness. The people cooperated because they were eager to discover new concepts. We demonstrated to them how to maintain and enhance the drainage system. With the aid of all communities, we built sanitary laboratories. We showed them several techniques for keeping the area surrounding their homes clean.

They fed us delicious food and entertained us with songs and dances around a bonfire every night. The camp was a huge success and a lot of fun. We formed long-lasting bonds with the villages.

questions.prompt_text: Expand the idea on your own on the following topic. Time and tide wait for none
questions.prompt_html:
Expand the idea on your own on the following topic.

Time and tide wait for none
questions.solution_html:
The proverb ‘Time and tide wait for none’ illustrates the significance of time. We may take time for granted but it keeps slipping away. Young or old, rich or poor, time does not discriminate; it does not wait for anyone! Likewise, tide, too, waits for none. Regardless of where you stand, the tide will take its course. It comes and goes when it has to. Similarly, life goes on, and to fulfill our dreams we need to make the most of every passing moment. We need to focus only on what matters and disregard anything which is detrimental to our development. A couple of stories based on the proverb ‘time and tide wait for none', for you to understand the true worth of the proverb.

Once there lived a poor farmer in a village in India. His whole family depended on the farm products he generated throughout the year. Like he does every year, the farmer had sown the crop, in a particular year. When the time of harvest came, he needed to go to the city to hire labourers for that. He started postponing this, thinking that he still has time, while all the other farmers have harvested their fields much in advance. Even his wife’s persistent persuasions couldn’t get the farmer to go to the city and get labourers. He was simply postponing it, thinking that nothing could happen with a delay of a couple of days. However, one day he decided that he would be going to the city. It so happened, that on the same night, a very strong storm came into the village. The winds were so strong that even big trees were uprooted.

Our poor farmer’s complete crop was destroyed in the storm. Regret not valuing time and harvesting the crops without delay. Had he done that, he wouldn’t have faced this situation. Nevertheless, it was useless to regret now, because time and tide wait for none, and they haven’t waited for our farmer.

Review of 'Rocketry'

The film 'Rocketry' was released on 1st July, 2022. This film is based on the life of one of India’s pioneering rocket scientists 'Nambi Narayanan', this biography chronicles his achievements, mad passion for the country's space mission, his unmatched dedication, and the accusation that eventually became the biggest personal and professional setback of his life.

The eventful life of Indian Space Research Organisation’s (ISRO) leading scientist and Padma Bhushan awardee Nambi Narayanan is so full of ups and downs that one wonders why it took so long for someone to come up with a full-fledged feature film on him. While it was attempted by a few, R Madhavan’s directorial debut which he also wrote and co-produced, finally saw the light of day. The film plays out in flashback as Nambi Narayanan (R Madhavan) narrates his life story to superstar Shah Rukh Khan in 2014. The crew filming this mammoth interview is cursing their luck for being stuck in the studio late at night for a ‘long and boring’ story of an old scientist. However, as Nambi begins talking, everyone including the host is riveted by his story.

The producer of the film is Sarita Madhavan, R. Madhavan, Varghese Moolan and Vijay Moolan whereas the director of the film is R. Madhavan. The character of nambi Narayan is played by R. Madhavan. The story spans Narayanan's days as a graduate student at Princeton University, before exploring his work as a scientist and the false espionage charges placed upon him.

R Madhavan relives Nambi Narayanan’s real life in reel with full conviction. From his make-up to dialogue delivery and expression, Madhavan becomes the man whose story he tells. Shah Rukh Khan looks dapper as ever and uses his trademark charm to play the role of an interviewer with a heart. He mirrors the conscience of a nation for a man, who dedicated his life to a cause against all odds. It is definitely a movie worth watching and gives respect to Nambi Narayan.

questions.solution_html:
Necessity of Social Awareness

Have you ever turned to look at surroundings while walking through your town or city? What have you noticed? You will quickly realize how important social awareness is for a variety of reasons if you just give it a little thought.

As we look around, we notice a lot of individuals going along the street, eating from plastic packets, and then discarding the empty packages. The biker only bends and spits in public when riding motorbikes. It is common to see garbage heaps lying around, and they emit a foul odor. Dogs, birds, and other animals then move these garbage heaps from one location to another.

Is this the type of environment we want for ourselves? Certainly not Out; it needs awareness and self-control. It must be realized that anytime we endeavour to preserve cleanliness and excellent hygiene around us, we are both benefiting ourselves and encouraging others to do the same. Rather than simply contemplating how our surroundings may change, we must take a proactive approach and begin demonstrating the correct path. There is a potential that others may begin to imitate us.

We must comprehend that even the smallest action taken in the right way may have a significant influence. Conditions that are dirty and unsanitary are particularly bad for us all. So let's start working together to avoid such situations.

questions.solution_html: Phileas Fogg’s final winning of the wager in Jules Verne’s 'Around the World in Eighty Days is connected with Aouda in a significant way. Aouda, who was rescued by Fogg and his companions during their journey, plays a crucial role in the story.
